title: Chaotic routing scenarios and mitigation notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a compact working-runbook embedded inside architecture thinking for extreme routing/control-plane anomalies. It's intentionally pragmatic: quick symptoms -> triage checklist -> targeted mitigations -> verification -> post-incident follow-ups. Designed for platform on-call, SRE, and on-shift platform eng. Not the canonical runbook (see linked Confluence) but a condensed set of scenarios we keep hitting during multi-region traffic shifts and capacity noise.

Assumptions and environment:
- Traffic fronted by edge gateways with regional controllers (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Control plane (CP) agents publish routing tables to edge, and CP leader election uses etcd/clusters per-region with cross-region reconciliation.
- Models are versioned and have small-compatible variants for graceful fallback.
- Key telemetry: per-region e2e p95 latency, token completion errors/s, CP leader_lag_ms, provisioning-queue-length, route-change-rate (rc/s), observed model-variant-fallback-rate.

Quick decision matrix (summary):
- Symptom: sudden increase in cross-region latency + route-change-rate spike -> suspect control-plane instability or reconciler loops.
  Action: pause automated rollouts (global), throttle route-change propagation, promote stable CP leader, assess etcd health.
- Symptom: regional saturation (compute queue rising) but CP healthy -> apply routing weight-shift to secondary regions + enable model-quantized fallbacks.
- Symptom: edge gateways misrouting (traffic blackholing) -> roll edge config to last-known-good, escalate to edge config owner, enable bypass route.
- Symptom: cascading failovers across regions -> enact global capacity circuit-breaker (limit new sessions), inform GTM + CS.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alert details: runbook-alert-id, time window, affected regions.
2) Slack channel: #oncall-platform and ping @sre-oncall.
3) Pull metrics:
   - dashboards/region-overview: p50/p95/p99, error-rate, rc/s
   - telemetry: cp-leader_lag_ms, etcd-raft-underreplicated, provisioning-queue-length
4) Query control-plane logs for leader elections: `kubectl -n controlplane logs --selector=app=cp-reconciler --since=10m`
5) Check route-change audit: `select * from route_audit where ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' order by ts desc limit 50`
6) If route-change-rate > 200rc/s and p95 increases, run `bin/cp-debug reconcile-dump --region <r> --last 1m` and capture payload sizes.

Mitigation recipes (targeted):
A. Reconciler storm (high rc/s, noisy reconciles)
   Steps:
   - Flip reconciler to read-only (global): `kubectl patch deployment cp-reconciler -n controlplane --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'` (prep saved golden manifest).
   - Revert recent config changes (if any): `git revert <config-PR>` and apply last-good via `kubectl apply -f stable-config.yaml`
   - If etcd reports underreplicated peers, restart the minority peers in order: stop -> wait 30s -> start, monitor raft index.
   Why: stops churn and reduces route-change flood while we stabilize leader/etcd.

B. Regional compute saturation (queues pile up, timeouts)
   Steps:
   - Move traffic weights away from affected region(s): use routing API `POST /api/v1/route/adjust` body `{region: "us-west-2", weight_delta: -0.30}` (internal auth token).
   - Enable quantized model variant for high-throughput endpoints: `deployments/scale --name transformer-x --variant quant8 --force`
   - Temporarily raise per-request CPU/GPU limits for critical routes if autoscaler hasn't reacted: `kubectl set resources deploy model-worker --limits=...`
   - If autoscaler is blocked due to control-plane write pressure, manually scale node pool via cloud console and tag nodes `need-drain=false` to avoid eviction.

C. Edge misrouting or blackholing
   Steps:
   - Rollback edge config to last-known-good: `edgemgr rollback --id <config-id>`
   - Enable bypass for affected prefix: `edgemgr route add --prefix /v1/ --target bypass-backend`
   - If config store is corrupt, switch to fail-open mode: `edgemgr set-mode --fail-open` and alert networking.

D. Cross-region reconciliation regressions (inconsistent route tables)
   Steps:
   - Pause cross-region sync: set `sync.enabled=false` in CP feature flags.
   - Snapshot route tables from each region: `route-inspect dump --region <r> --output routes-<r>.json`
   - Run diff tool: `route-diff routes-us-west-2.json routes-eu-west-1.json` and identify divergent prefixes.
   - Apply manual reconciliation for critical prefixes: `route-inspect apply --file reconciled-prefixes.json --mode manual`

Communication play (templates):
- Incident channel opener (Slack):
  Title: [P0] Routing/CP degradation - {regions} - {short symptom}
  Body: "We are investigating increased route churn and latency in {regions}. On-call: {owner}. Initial mitigations: paused automated rollouts and throttled reconciles. Next updates every 10m. Impacted customers: {approx list}."
- Customer-facing status blurb (status.redwood.ai):
  "We are investigating an elevated error rate for inference requests in {region}. Traffic is being shifted to alternate regions while we stabilize the control plane. No customer data exposure. More updates shortly."

Escalation matrix: who to call
- Oncall SRE (first) -> Platform eng lead (Marcus Li) -> Network infra (Sophie Chen) -> Model infra (Emily Zhang) -> Eng manager / Pager for execs if > 60m unresolved or >= high customer impact.
Phone numbers and pager links are in team roster (internal).

Verification checklist (before closing):
- Route-change-rate back to baseline for 30m.
- p95 latency within SLA +/- 20% for 30m.
- No reconcilers in crashloop, CP leader stable > 60s.
- Customer error-rate normalized and affected customer list notified.
- Postmortem owner assigned within 24h.

Post-incident actions (ASAP within 72h):
- Root cause analysis with cp logs and etcd raft tracing.
- Add pre-commit guard to block rapid config changes when rc/s > threshold.
- Improve visibility: add histogram of route churn per-prefix and integrate into alerting.
- Run a tabletop exercise mimicking the exact failure path and validate manual reconciliation steps.

Known caveats and noisy false-positives:
- Short-lived spikes from synthetic load tests that hit reconciler endpoints can mimic CP storms; check the test-run ledger first.
- Autoscaler events can create transient route changes as nodes come up; correlate with cloud provider events.

Short checklist for after-hours on-call (one-liners):
- If route-change-rate > 200rc/s and p95 > baseline+200ms -> pause reconciler + throttle CP API.
- If provisioning-queue > 500 -> shift weights + enable quantized variants.
- If edge returns 502s for large token streams -> rollback edge config -> enable bypass route.

Open questions / follow-ups (work items):
- Investigate automated circuit-breaker that can detect multi-region cascading and automatically cap new sessions. (JIRA-OPS-1530)
- Add quick CLI to snapshot route tables and submit to central incident ticket (owner: Rafael).
- Revisit leader-election timeouts for cp agents across regions; current defaults appear aggressive under network skew.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep `stable-config.yaml` in a protected branch and tag releases with config-hash.
- Consider small canary window for cross-region sync; currently we push everything global and that feels brittle.

Last tested run (dry run): 2026-01-14 by Marcus Li — simulated reconcilers storm, validated pause+rollback sequence reduced rc/s from ~320 to <15 within 120s.

Attachment ideas for canonical runbook:
- One-page cheat sheet for oncall with 4 quick commands (pause reconciler, rollback edge, shift weights, snapshot routes).
- Example postmortem template focusing on route churn metrics.

If you're editing: mark CHANGES at top with date and initials.

- Priya
